Diagnosis: `_equal_sign` was `=[^\S\r\n]*`, greedily consuming whitespace after `=`. For `KEY= # note`, the value reader then started at `#`, so `parse_unquoted_value`'s `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part)` saw no preceding whitespace and returned `"# note"` instead of `""`.

Change plan (applied): reverted `_equal_sign` to `=` in `src/dotenv/parser.py` (line 24). Now the whitespace after `=` reaches `parse_unquoted_value`, whose existing `\s+#.*` strip yields `""` for `KEY= # note`, `KEY=  # note`, `KEY=\t# note`, and `export KEY = # note`. `KEY=#literal` and `KEY=a#b` keep their `#` (no preceding whitespace). Quoting, exports, and ordinary `# comment` lines are unaffected. Only `src/dotenv/parser.py` was edited; no tests/docs/deps touched.
